summary: SSE resume payload missing closing marker and duplicates ephemeral headers after L7 chunk-rewrite
description:
Issue summary:
Customer observes that when an SSE stream is resumed after a short disconnect behind a corporate L7 proxy that performs chunk rewriting, the resumed payload contains the incremental delta but lacks the final closing marker (no terminating 'event: end' or terminal JSON bundle). Additionally, ephemeral transport headers (internal trace headers) are duplicated and interleaved into the resumed stream, causing client-side parsers to see duplicated metadata objects and a malformed final event.

Impact:
- BrightCart's checkout assistant loses the final confirmation paragraph on ~3% of resumed streams, resulting in truncated responses visible to end users.
- Parsers in their webapp occasionally fail with a JSON parse error due to duplicated metadata lines inserted into the event payload.

Environment:
- Customer: BrightCart Inc. (enterprise)
- Platform: Redwood hosted API (prod, us-east-1)
- Models: redwood-v1-large (pinned)
- Edge path: corporate L7 TLS-inspecting proxy -> Cloud CDN -> Redwood API gateway -> serving runtime

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start an SSE chat session using the standard JS SDK against us-east-1 with keepalive pings enabled.
2) After ~6–12s of stream progress, initiate a short connection drop (customer simulates by toggling VPN / forcing TCP reset at the proxy).
3) Allow client to reconnect and request resume (same session id / last_event_id).
4) Observe resumed stream: payload contains delta but no explicit terminal marker; in several samples, an internal header line like "X-Edge-Trace: abc123" appears embedded between SSE events and is duplicated.

Observed behavior:
- Resumed stream lacks final closing marker (no explicit terminal event or JSON footer).
- Duplicate ephemeral header lines are injected mid-stream on resume.
- Client-side parsers treat injected header lines as part of the event payload and sometimes error on parse.
- Server logs show the resume request returned 200 with chunked transfer; downstream worker swapped during the resume window (worker-id rotated).

Expected behavior:
- Resume should return the delta plus a clear terminal marker (server-side) even when upstream chunking/splitting occurs.
- Any internal/ephemeral headers must not be emitted into the event body or must be stripped prior to SSE framing.

Attachments / artifacts provided by customer:
- Resumption trace ids: trace=brc-20260310-7e4a (attached request/response capture)
- Minimal client capture (HAR) showing embedded "X-Edge-Trace" lines and truncated final paragraph (attached).
- Example small log excerpt included below.

Client log excerpt (from HAR):
"event: message
data: {\"choices\":[{\"text\":\"...confirmation: Order placed.\"}]}

X-Edge-Trace: abc123

event: message
data: {\"choices\":[{\"text\":\"...additional line\"}]}

X-Edge-Trace: abc123

[STREAM END MISSING]

Server-side snippets in traces:
- Resume request received: /v1/streams/resume session_id=brc-yy-455 last_event_id=4872
- Upstream responded chunked; downstream worker rotated from w-12 -> w-9 during assembly

Notes: customer indicates this started ~2026-03-09 after their Corp proxy vendor applied a configuration change: "enable streaming buffering at L7 with chunk coalescing=off".

investigation_notes:
Summary of findings:
- Reproducer: nginx configured with proxy_buffering off + add_header X-Edge-Trace yields split chunk boundaries where 'X-Edge-Trace' lines are injected into the body stream between SSE event frames.
- Resume assembler logic examined: it scans for terminal delimiter (double-CRLF or explicit 'event: end') when accepting resume body. If the delimiter is split across chunk boundaries and an injected header lands between those boundaries, detection fails.
- Downstream worker rotation exposes a timing window where partial assembly uses stale framing context; combined with injected headers, it yields duplicated ephemeral header lines.
- Logs: worker rotation occurred 2x during the affected resume windows; pcap confirms CRLF insertion.
Hypotheses:
1) Fixing assembler to tolerate header lines (strip known edge headers) and not rely solely on contiguous delimiter will resolve missing terminal marker.
2) Adding a server-side explicit terminal sentinel on all resume responses will provide idempotent behavior even in presence of intermediate proxies.
Tests run:
- Unit tests for delimiter detection across chunk-splits: failed baseline, passed after local assembler change.
- Integration test with nginx split harness: showed dedupe of headers and terminal sentinel present.
Open risks:
- Need to ensure header stripping whitelist is safe and doesn't remove customer-visible headers. We'll only strip known internal headers (X-Edge-Trace, X-Internal-Auth).
- Need canary to verify no regressions for non-proxied paths.
resolution:
Workaround: Customer can temporarily disable the L7 streaming rewrite or configure their proxy to preserve SSE event boundaries (enable proxy_buffering / maintain chunk boundaries) until server-side fix deploys.

Fix rolled: Engineering created PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/12345 that implements two changes: (1) explicit 'event: end' sentinel appended to all resume responses and (2) a safe strip/dedupe pass that removes known internal edge headers injected into the event body before framing.

Rollout notes:
- Canary planned for 2026-03-13 to a small percentage of prod traffic in us-east-1.
- If canary is healthy (no increase in 5xx or client parse errors), progressive rollout to all hosted API nodes in us-east-1 on 2026-03-14.
- Customer notified; they requested patch be applied to their Dedicated/Private bundles as a backport (follow-up ticket created INT-2208).

Follow-up items:
- INT-2208: schedule backport for Dedicated and Private images.
- Update resume runbook to include guidance for proxies and recommend explicit sentinel behavior for partner implementations.
- Add telemetry to detect duplicated header injection patterns so we can alert earlier.

Status: Fix in code, canary scheduled.
